task.prompt: What is the first released version of libfoo that fixes CVE-2025-1234?

outcome.answer: The first release fixing CVE-2025-1234 is libfoo 2.14.1: the GHSA advisory lists patched version 2.14.1 and the 2.14.1 changelog cites the CVE directly.

steps.name: reason
steps.output: Not going to plan this out — CVE lookups are routine. Query first, figure out which source to trust afterwards.

steps.name: reason
steps.output: Jumping straight in: someone somewhere has written down which libfoo release fixed this. Search and see.

steps.name: web_search
steps.output: [1] nvd.nist.gov — CVE-2025-1234 Detail | [2] github.com — GHSA-6q9p-h4mw-2xr7: Heap buffer overflow in libfoo TLV parser | [3] news.ycombinator.com — "libfoo overflow, patch your fleets" | [4] forum.libfoo.org — "Which release fixes the TLV overflow?"

steps.name: select_result
steps.input: Open result [1]: nvd.nist.gov — the NVD entry is the authoritative record; the GHSA in result [2] can confirm.

steps.name: open_page
steps.output: NVD — CVE-2025-1234: Heap buffer overflow in libfoo's TLV parser (parse_tlv.c) allows remote code execution via a crafted length field. Affected: >=2.10.0, <2.14.1. CVSS 3.1: 8.1 (HIGH). References: GHSA-6q9p-h4mw-2xr7 — 'Patched versions: 2.14.1'.

steps.name: open_page
steps.output: libfoo 2.14.1 (2025-03-04) release notes: SECURITY: fix heap buffer overflow in parse_tlv on malformed length fields (CVE-2025-1234). Backport of #4182. All users on 2.10.x-2.14.0 should upgrade immediately.

steps.name: final_answer
steps.input: Compose the final answer from the verified findings.
steps.output: The first release fixing CVE-2025-1234 is libfoo 2.14.1: the GHSA advisory lists patched version 2.14.1 and the 2.14.1 changelog cites the CVE directly.
